title: A flow mapping of 1,600 pairs with the same key must be refused without growing quadratically
notes: Every pair has the key `a`, so the mapping is invalid: the keys of a mapping must be unique, and no result is allowed. Reading the 10 KB input must take memory in proportion to its size. A reader that records an error for every duplicate in a structure that grows with the square of the pairs, or copies its state at each one, needs hundreds of megabytes here (measured over repeated runs at 1,600 pairs: one reader 194–196 MB, another 248–259 MB; both grow three to five times for each doubling of the pairs) while readers that stop at the first duplicate stay under 15 MB. The bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Input: `{`, then `a: b, ` 1,600 times, then `}`. The refusal is a duplicate-key error (YAML 1.2.2 section 3.2.1.1: the keys of a mapping are unique), or a limit error.

provenance.reference: Readers that report every duplicate key of a mapping, or keep per-key state, in memory that grows with the square of the number of pairs.
